National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
351 AM EDT Sun Aug 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Nothing.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Warmer and more humid today with isolated afternoon
  thunderstorms possible.

- 2) Late summer heat returns this week.

- 3) Thunderstorm chances increase this week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Warmer and more humid today with isolated afternoon
thunderstorms possible.

Low level moisture has increased over the area early this
morning as evidence of low clouds on satellite imagery and sfc 
dewpoints now in the mid 60s compared to the mid 50s yesterday.
High pressure building to the south of the area today will 
allow for a warmer and more unstable air mass. A developing 
surface trof may be able to spark a few thunderstorms this 
afternoon in an increasingly hot, humid, and unstable air mass.
Thunderstorms should dissipate quickly as we approach sunset.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Late summer heat returns this week.

Guidance remains steadfast on late summer heat returning to end 
meteorological summer (June 1-August 31) and begin meteorological 
autumn (September 1-November 30).

A strong mid-level ridge will build across the southern CONUS and 
into the Mid-Atlantic, then persist through at least the middle of 
the week. Some guidance has been trending towards having the ridge 
axis a bit further south and west, which would lower heights a bit 
and introduce more chances for showers and thunderstorms at times in 
large scale NW flow aloft. This lends to a bit of spread in the 
temperature forecast, especially if any back-door surface cold 
fronts slide into the region by mid/late week.

Despite the uncertainties, it remains likely that high temperatures 
will reach the lower to middle 90s for much of the region for much 
of the new work week. Latest guidance indicates potential for 
temperatures in the upper 90s to near 100 mid week, so long as 
it is not disrupted by cloud cover or convection. Depending on 
smaller scale details, dew points could end up a little higher 
or lower than currently progged which will ultimately affect how
high heat index values get. Values approaching Heat Advisory 
criteria (100-104 west of the Blue Ridge, 105-109 east of the 
Blue Ridge) are possible.

Temperatures may begin to moderate by next weekend as a cold front 
crosses the region.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Thunderstorm chances increase this week.

Disturbances rounding a ridge to the south and west in NW flow aloft 
will introduce shower and thunderstorm chances at times this 
week. The timing and amplitude of these waves have very low 
predictability beyond a couple days in advance (at best). But 
the general theme will be enhanced lift and shear clashing with 
an increasingly hot and unstable airmass over or near the Mid- 
Atlantic. AI/ML guidance has broad elevated probabilities of 
severe weather much of this week, particularly Tuesday through 
Thursday (and possibly Friday). Guidance is currently most keen 
on a shortwave impulse passing just to the north on Wednesday.

It should be noted that there is a conditional potential for one or 
more organized clusters of strong to severe storms at some point 
this week. The most likely time currently appears to be around 
mid week, but changes are to be expected at this time range.

Storm chances may linger into next weekend as a cold front
crosses.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...

MVFR cigs this morning, scattering out after daybreak. Isold
afternoon t-storms today, mainly west of I-95. Have a PROB30
group for MRB and nothing elsewhere. Better chances of
thunderstorms Mon and Tue.

Episodic SHRA/TSRA (highest chc in the aftn/eve) as well as AM 
fog/low clouds could bring intermittent restrictions much of
this week. Winds generally S/SW AOB 15 kts.

&&

.MARINE...

SCA has been issued for this evening into early Monday for 20kt
gusts in southerly channeling. 

Additional bouts of channeling may be possible by mid to late 
week. Chances of thunderstorms increase through the week, with 
stronger and more organized storms possible especially by mid 
week.
